Flexible connection agreement · Pillar 4

Economic arrangements

How is curtailed energy valued and compensated?

Jump to feedback

Pillar philosophy

How to think about this pillar

This pillar allocates the economic consequences of curtailment: compensation, alternative value streams, consequences of non-compliance and responsibility for imbalances.

Main question

How is curtailed energy valued and compensated?

Pillar map

Dimensions

CompensationValue stackingNon-compliance penaltyImbalance responsibility

Design tutorial

Read the pillar as a design sequence

Review the economic layer together with tariffs and local markets so that the same flexibility is not unintentionally charged or rewarded twice.

1. Define curtailment compensation

State whether compensation exists and how its value is determined.

2. Define permitted value stacking

Record whether energy affected by curtailment may be traded through bilateral contracts, local flexibility markets or other channels.

3. Allocate non-compliance and imbalance risk

State consequences for exceeding limits and identify who carries imbalance responsibility when curtailment changes schedules.

Key language

Terms to keep consistent

Use these short definitions consistently when comparing schemes or discussing this pillar.

Compensation

The payment rule, if any, that applies when the user is curtailed under the flexible connection.

Value stacking

The ability to combine the flexible connection with other commercial arrangements, such as bilateral contracts or local flexibility markets, subject to compatibility rules.

Non-compliance

A breach of the agreed flexible-connection limits or required control conditions.

Balance Responsible Party (BRP)

The party financially responsible for the difference between physical energy and nominated energy within the imbalance settlement period.

Imbalance responsibility

The rule assigning financial responsibility for imbalances created when curtailment changes the scheduled injection or withdrawal.

Double compensation / double charging

A coordination risk where the same flexibility or curtailment effect is rewarded or charged more than once through overlapping mechanisms.

Expert questionnaire

Evaluate this pillar

Does this pillar make the allocation of curtailment value, market opportunity and financial responsibility sufficiently clear to prevent conflicting incentives?

  1. Are compensation mechanisms, value stacking opportunities and imbalance responsibility independent dimensions or should some of them be merged?
  2. Does the pillar adequately capture how risks and rewards are distributed between the customer and the SO?
  3. Does this pillar make it possible to identify situations where double charging or double compensation may occur?
  4. Do the compensation options (fixed, set by the local flexibility market, local-market indexed, none) cover all possible ways of compensating curtailed users?
